currentContext.business: JK Cement Limited manufactures and sells grey cement, white cement and wall putty in India, and through its Fujairah-based subsidiaries manufactures and sells white cement, clinker and drymix for the Middle East, GCC and export markets. Its grey cement capacity rose from 24.34 MnTPA as on 31st March 2025 to 32.26 MnTPA as on 31st March 2026 through greenfield grinding units, brownfield additions, debottlenecking and the acquisition of a controlling stake in Saifco Cement, serving priority regions from Jammu and Kashmir to Eastern and Southern India. Demand is drawn from housing, infrastructure and the industrial and commercial segments, with a growing value-added portfolio that includes paints through JK Maxx Paints Limited.

currentContext.expansion: FY 2025-26 was a heavy delivery year: grey cement capacity grew from 24.34 MnTPA as on 31st March 2025 to 32.26 MnTPA as on 31st March 2026, and the Company states the additions were delivered on time and within budget. The programme comprised roughly 6 MnTPA of expansion in Central India — a 3.3 MnTPA clinker facility commissioned at Panna plus 6 MnTPA of cement capacity made up of the greenfield Buxar grinding unit (3 MnTPA) and 1 MnTPA each at Panna, Prayagraj and Hamirpur — alongside debottlenecking of 1 MnTPA at Muddapur and 0.5 MnTPA at Ujjain, and the acquisition of a 60% stake in Saifco Cement Private Limited (0.42 MnTPA), which extended the footprint towards Jammu and Kashmir. Panna's expansion with split grinding locations is credited with making the Company a strong player in the Central region. A further 7 MnTPA of greenfield grey cement capacity is under execution in North India, to be commissioned by H1 FY28: a 4 MnTPA clinker unit together with a 3 MnTPA cement grinding unit at Jaisalmer, described as progressing as planned and scheduled for completion in H1 FY 2027-28; a 2 MnTPA split grinding unit at Bikaner expected to be commissioned in H1 FY28; and a 2 MnTPA split grinding unit at Bathinda, Punjab, where 100% of the land has been acquired and orders for the main plant and machinery have been completed, also scheduled for H1 FY28. The Jaisalmer unit is expected to consolidate and improve the Company's market share in the North region. The total project cost for this North India expansion is estimated at approximately Rs 4,805 Crores, of which Rs 914 Crores had been incurred as on 31st March 2026. Beyond grey cement, a wall putty plant of 6 Lakhs tonnes capacity is under construction at Nathdwara, progressing as per schedule and expected to be completed in Q2 FY27, at an estimated project cost of Rs 195 Crores of which Rs 100 Crores had been incurred as on 31st March 2026. A further 10-12 MnTPA of additional grey cement capacity is under planning, supporting the stated journey to 50 MnTPA of grey cement capacity by FY30, underpinned by strategic acquisition of limestone and coal reserves. During the year the Company also incorporated JK Cement Foundation (wholly owned, April 8, 2025) and the step-down foreign subsidiary JK Drychem Industries LLC (October 6, 2025), and amalgamated wholly owned subsidiary Toshali Cements Private Limited with the Company effective October 15, 2025 pursuant to NCLT approval. Industry context cited by management: ~65 MnTPA was added across the industry in FY 2025-26 to ~730 MnTPA installed capacity, roughly 75 MnTPA more is anticipated in FY 2026-27, and the operating rate is likely to moderate from ~74% to around 72%.
currentContext.mdna: Cement demand rebounded in FY 2025-26 with the industry expanding by 7-8%, led by rural housing, industrial and commercial segments while infrastructure activity remained steady; demand is expected to surge 7-8% again in the upcoming year with a marginal uptick in infrastructure.|Housing is the largest demand pool at 57% of segment-wise contribution, followed by infrastructure at 30% and industrial and commercial at 13%.|Housing demand is expected to grow ~7%, driven by rural housing on the back of GST reforms, lower interest rates, PM Dhan Dhaanya Krishi Yojana and improved PMAY-G execution, with urban housing moderate due to a real estate slowdown.|Government allocations support the demand base: Rs 1.94 Lakhs Crore for rural development and Rs 1.45 Lakhs Crore for affordable housing in FY 2026-27, up 53% and 25% over revised FY 2025-26 targets, and a 182% increase in the PMAY-Urban allocation.|Infrastructure grew ~8% in FY 2025-26 and infrastructure capex for the upcoming year is estimated 17.7% higher, with higher allocations to Road Transport & Highways, Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana, NHAI and Railways.|Industrial and commercial demand is underpinned by private investment, PLI schemes and commercial real estate, with average annual industrial capex of around Rs 7.1 Lakhs Crores expected between FY 2025-26 and FY 2029-30 and PLI-linked and emerging sectors accounting for ~27% of projected investment.|Supply-side pressure: the industry added ~65 MnTPA in FY 2025-26 to ~730 MnTPA installed capacity, with roughly 75 MnTPA anticipated in FY 2026-27, so the operating rate is likely to moderate from ~74% to around 72% in FY 2026-27; nearly 250 MnTPA is expected to be added between FY 2026-27 and FY 2030-31 to reach ~975 MnTPA by end FY 2030-31.|Management expects structural demand tailwinds to remain intact from infrastructure creation aspirations, accelerating private capex, rural and affordable housing schemes, rapid urbanisation, data centres and commercial real estate.|Cost headwinds flagged by management: escalating geopolitical tensions in West Asia have raised imported pet coke and diesel costs and cement bag costs, amplified by rupee depreciation, directly affecting margins and competitiveness; the response is operational efficiencies, energy-mix optimisation, sourcing diversification and calibrated pricing actions.|Macro backdrop: India's GDP is projected to moderate to ~6.6% in FY 2026-27 from an estimated 7.7% in FY 2025-26, with El Nino-driven below-normal rainfall (around 90% of Long Period Average) and crude oil over $110 per barrel cited as risks.|Volume milestone as a mix driver: grey cement volumes crossed 20 million tonnes for the first time in a full financial year, and capacity crossed 30 MnTPA, supporting deeper market penetration and cost competitiveness.|Most planned industry capacity additions are being undertaken by large and mid-sized players with cash surpluses and comfortable gearing, giving them flexibility to raise debt for expansion.

risks.risk: Industry overcapacity compressing utilisation and pricing
risks.note: The industry added ~65 MnTPA in FY 2025-26 to reach ~730 MnTPA installed capacity and roughly 75 MnTPA more is anticipated in FY 2026-27; despite continued demand growth the operating rate is likely to moderate from ~74% to around 72% in FY 2026-27, with nearly 250 MnTPA more expected between FY 2026-27 and FY 2030-31 to reach ~975 MnTPA. The eastern region, followed by the northern and western regions, is expected to take the largest share of additions - the same regions into which the Company is expanding.

risks.risk: Energy and fuel cost inflation driven by crude oil and geopolitical disruption
risks.note: Crude oil prices are cited at over $110 per barrel against a March 26 exit of $85, and rising geopolitical turmoil in West Asia including the war between the US and Iran has raised concerns over energy security and price volatility. Given India's substantial dependence on imported crude, sustained disruptions to global energy supply chains could lead to higher input costs and elevated inflation - a direct cost exposure for a fuel- and freight-intensive cement producer.

Management notes that exchange rate volatility and depreciation of the Indian rupee could further push up inflation by increasing the cost of energy and other essential imported items. The Company also has AED- and TZS-denominated overseas operations whose results are translated for reporting.

risks.risk: Monsoon / El Nino risk to rural demand
risks.note: El Nino in the Pacific is described as a significant threat to economic activity in FY 2026-27, with IMD-projected rainfall around 90% of the Long Period Average and a 60% probability of a below-normal season, raising concerns for agriculture, food inflation and the broader economy. Rural housing is the principal driver of the housing segment on which cement demand most depends.

risks.risk: Macro slowdown - India GDP growth moderating
risks.note: GDP growth is estimated at 7.7% in FY 2025-26 but is projected to moderate to 6.6% per the RBI revised estimate in FY 2026-27, amid evolving global economic and warm climate conditions, geopolitical uncertainties and external inflationary pressures.

risks.risk: Demand concentration in housing and government-funded construction
risks.note: Segment-wise contribution is 57% housing, 30% infrastructure and 13% industrial and commercial. A large part of the demand narrative rests on government budget allocations - rural development, PMAY-G and PMAY-U, Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana, NHAI and Railways - which makes volumes sensitive to fiscal priorities and execution rather than purely private demand.

The February 2026 India-US trade agreement cut US tariffs on Indian goods from 50% to 18% and affected 55% of India's $87 billion of exports to the US, with India agreeing to move towards zero tariffs and halt Russian crude purchases; world trade volume growth is expected to fall from 4.6% in 2025 to 1.9% in 2026. Trade policy uncertainty feeds directly into the input-cost and currency channels the Company is exposed to.

risks.risk: Realisation pressure in the white/putty business and loss-making newer subsidiaries
risks.note: The Directors' Report states that putty realisation remained under pressure during the year even as white cement and wall putty volumes grew, and that the paints subsidiary JK Maxx Paints Limited and the newly acquired J. K. Cement Saifco Private Limited were loss-making in FY 2025-26 - the diversification into value-added building materials is not yet self-funding.

one-line thesis: Volume-led, margin-pressured quarter: grey volumes +19% YoY (combined +18%) drove standalone net sales +23% to Rs 3,786 cr, but EBITDA/ton fell to Rs 982 (from Rs 1,229 YoY) on the sharpest fuel/energy shock in memory, so PAT slipped to Rs 291 cr (from Rs 333 cr). The entire growth engine is Central India (new Bihar grinding + capacity), where JK gained share; North & South are capacity-constrained (~85-90% utilization). Management held all expansion timelines (Jaisalmer H1FY28, 40 MT FY28, 50 MT FY30) and flagged a further ~Rs 150/ton cost rise in Q2 (fuel peaking) before relief — while paint hit EBITDA break-even and RMC scaled from 5 → 17 plants.

> Adjustments: Q1 carried **~Rs 50 cr extra (pre-poned) maintenance** (kiln red-spot timing) — no volume loss (large clinker stock buffer). Incentive income ~Rs 50 cr this quarter (GST-cut compressed). Fuel mix Q1: 40% pet-coke / 45% Indian coal / balance AFR. Paint Rs 125 cr revenue sits mostly in standalone (Maxx brand); Acro brand direct from subsidiary.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Grey volume 22.5-23 MT FY27** (double-digit growth; H2 "may not sustain" Q1's ~19% as base builds — implies ~6-7% for remaining quarters; management will "maximize" if demand holds).
- **Cost +~Rs 150/ton in Q2** (~Rs 100 fuel + ~Rs 50 diesel/other); **fuel cost peaks in Q2** (~1.75 Rs/Kcal from 1.53), decline thereafter; packaging flat/lower; Q2 maintenance similar/marginally lower.
- **Capacity: 40 MT by FY28, 50 MT by FY30** — "on schedule, no plans to reschedule." Jaisalmer greenfield (6 MT) commissioning **H1FY28**; Bhatinda grinding progressing; 2nd Punjab split-grinding land acquired.
- **Wall putty +0.6 MTPA (Nathdwara) commissioning Q2FY27** (reduce toll-manufacturing dependence; grow putty double-digit).
- **Panna Line 2 debottleneck 3.3 → 4 MT clinker this fiscal (FY27)**; no clinker shortage foreseen for Central India.
- **Paint (JK Maxx):** FY27 revenue Rs 500-550 cr (EBITDA break-even Q1 achieved, 3rd year of ops); FY28 EBITDA margin 5-7% with topline +~Rs 150 cr; investment capped at Rs 600 cr (core-business priority).
- **RMC:** 17 plants now → **50 by FY27, 100 by FY28**; FY27 revenue ~Rs 250 cr (maybe 300); ~breakeven FY27 (single-digit loss); structural margin only 4-7%.
- **Capex Rs 3,500 cr FY27, ~Rs 1,200 cr FY28** (+ next-leg expansion additional).
- **Coal blocks:** Mahan (larger) commissioning **end-FY28**, second ~1 yr later — substantial fuel-cost saving + risk reduction.
- **Incentives:** ~Rs 225-250 cr FY29, back to **~Rs 300 cr/yr** once new units (Buxar/Panna) restore eligibility.
- **Green power 75% by FY30** (ramp ~4-5%/yr from next year); thermal-substitution 35% FY30 target being reworked for new fuel mix.
order book & pipeline: Not an order-book business — spot cement. Demand read: prices flat/steady in Q1; no monsoon price drop expected this year despite seasonality (cost pass-through on geopolitical energy). Central India is the only growth headroom (North/South capacity-constrained). White-cement demand got a one-off lift as UAE imports were disrupted (geopolitical shipping). Infra/housing demand supportive.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Grey cement:** +19% YoY, all growth from Central India (new Bihar grinding); share gained in Central, held in North/South; North & South ~85-90% utilization (out of capacity). Panna overall utilization >65%.
- **White cement + putty:** white +11% YoY (+~28-29% by another cut, +~4% QoQ realization) — UAE-import disruption gave extra volume; competitiveness in putty/white will normalize. Nathdwara +0.6 MTPA putty (Q2) to cut toll dependence.
- **Paints (JK Maxx):** Q1 revenue Rs 125 cr, EBITDA break-even (up from ~Rs 100 cr/qtr prior 3 quarters, Rs 380 cr FY26); FY27 target Rs 500-550 cr; uses the JK Cement putty platform (service-charge model); Acro + Maxx brands. Helps putty volumes.

themes.title: Cement demand & pricing recovery
themes.need: Q1FY27 turned cement from a pricing story into a volume-share-plus-fuel-cost story. ULTRACEMCO grew domestic grey volume +13.1% YoY against an estimated ~7-8% industry, delivered its first Rs 5,000cr+ April-June EBITDA (Rs 5,146cr) with EBITDA/ton held above Rs 1,200, and crossed 200.1 MT domestic capacity a year early - but guided Q2FY27 cost UP ~Rs 130-140/ton and pinned the Rs 1,400/ton consolidated target to Q4FY28. The fuel shock, not price, is the swing factor: JKCEMENT's EBITDA/ton fell to Rs 982 from Rs 1,229 YoY despite +19% grey volume, DALBHARAT flagged pet coke 'surged to nearly $160/t' versus a pre-war $110-115, and NUVOCO defended INR 1,079/ton EBITDA only by cutting petcoke from 37% to 27% of fuel mix in a single quarter. Consolidation is visibly compounding (INDIACEM EBITDA/ton Rs 386->400->509->603 across four quarters; DALBHARAT closed Jaypee at Rs 2,850cr EV with Chunar operational and Rewa on trial within 50 days) even as DALBHARAT slipped its 75mt milestone from FY27 to FY28. SHREECEM/RAMCOCEM/JKLAKSHMI/JSWCEMENT/STARCEMENT/BIRLACORPN ride the same volume + consolidation axis.
themes.driver: Q2FY27 is the guided cost trough - ULTRACEMCO ~Rs 130-140/ton, JKCEMENT ~Rs 150/ton and BIRLACORPN Rs 70-80/ton of incremental cost; then fuel-mix agility (NUVOCO's petcoke swing) and whether DALBHARAT's ~Rs 150/t of procurement savings is really 'permanent, not timing'.
